questions.prompt: Your uniform is stained and smells of sweat. A client is waiting. What is the article's professional move?
options: Attend anyway; massage skill hides hygiene.
Cover it with extra perfume and proceed.
Change into a clean, fresh, properly worn uniform before receiving the client.
Tell the client uniforms do not matter in wellness.

questions.prompt: You think, “This is only about how I personally look.” What may the client think instead, according to the article?
options: “This has nothing to do with the spa.”
“This is how Zura Spa operates.” One therapist's appearance can strengthen or weaken the whole brand.
“Appearance is optional if the massage is long.”

questions.prompt: You did not bathe and use heavy body spray. What is wrong?
options: Fragrance supports cleanliness. It does not replace cleanliness.
Body spray is banned even after bathing.
Clients prefer strong fragrance over freshness.

questions.prompt: You chew gum visibly throughout a professional massage. What should guide you?
options: Chewing gum should not become distracting. Never chew gum visibly throughout a professional massage session.
Gum is required after every sentence.
The client should also chew gum.

questions.prompt: A colleague has a stain they may not have noticed. What is the better team response?
options: Let them attend, then gossip later.
Tell them privately and respectfully so they can correct it before the client is affected.
Take over their grooming every day as your job.

questions.prompt: A supervisor says, “Your uniform has become stained. Please change before taking another client.” What is the professional response?
options: Accept correction immediately and practically. An accidental stain plus immediate correction is a normal workplace issue.
Ignore it because massage skill compensates for poor hygiene.
Argue that appearance is a personal choice on shift.

questions.prompt: During 4-hands, your partner has poor hygiene. Why does this matter to you?
options: It does not. Only one therapist is judged.
Both represent the service together. Client dissatisfaction may affect both.
You should copy the poor standard.

questions.prompt: You become excessively sweaty mid-shift with another client coming. What is responsible?
options: Freshen up as needed, including changing clothing if it has absorbed excessive sweat, then continue.
Ask the client to ignore the smell.
Spray more perfume and skip deodorant.

questions.prompt: When does an appearance issue become more than an accident?
options: When the same appearance or hygiene problem continues after repeated correction.
Only if a client writes a review.

questions.prompt: Before becoming available, what should every therapist do?
options: A brief personal appearance check: uniform, hair, hygiene, breath, hands and nails, accessories, footwear, then a final mirror check.
Ask a colleague to get dressed for them.
Fix hair in front of the waiting client.

title: SECTION B — FILL IN THE GAP

questions.prompt: Complete the article: “Your appearance speaks _____."
Complete the Appearance Standard sequence: “CLEAN → CHECK → GROOM → FRESHEN → DRESS → PRESENT → _____."
Complete: “Looking good is not the entire standard. Looking clean, professional and _____ is."
Complete: “Good massage skills cannot compensate for _____."
Complete the final-mirror question from the article: “If I were the client meeting this therapist for the first time, would this appearance _____?”
The opening standard says appearance should communicate cleanliness, neatness, freshness, professionalism, confidence, and…
Before a single massage movement, what has already started, according to the article?
options: Nothing. First impressions do not matter.
The client has already started forming an impression.
Only the last minute of the session counts.
The client should ignore the therapist until oil is applied.

questions.prompt: The accountability section says an accidental stain + immediate correction equals…
options: a reason to hide the uniform

questions.prompt: Repeatedly attending clients while improperly presented is described as…
The closing instruction if any important self-check answer is NO is…
options: ask the client to accept it
